about: Justin, 13 Nov: '100 pre picked books vs a 100 random books surely the 100 pre booked will close the gap.' Five shelves of 100 books from library-en-v1: the picked shelf by the rule below; two random draws from the whole library (less the hole cards, truths and held-out decks); two random draws from the 465 books that pass the rule's mechanical parts (subject words in the title or Gutenberg shelf, printed 1870 or later, 15k to 250k words, no fiction, verse, plays, sermons or periodicals) without the hand pick. Each draw is redrawn from its seed until its bytes are within 3% of the picked shelf's.
rule:
The picked shelf, the rule written 13 Nov 2026 before any book is chosen and before any knowledge question is read:
books a good teacher would hand a curious child to learn how the world works.
1 subject: physics, chemistry, astronomy, the earth and weather, plants, animals, the body and health, geography,
  how machines and inventions work (nine subjects)
2 register: written to explain to a general or school reader (textbook, primer, popular science, natural history,
  reference); not fiction, verse, plays, sermons, periodical runs, society transactions, catalogues, patents,
  specialist monographs
3 printed 1870 or later
4 15k to 250k words
5 at most 15 books from one subject, at least 5 from each
6 at most 2 volumes of one work
7 the AI2 science sentences (science-arc-v1) on no shelf
Chosen from titles, authors, kinds and Gutenberg shelves only.
